title: Forfait
tagline: Turn a 60-day invoice into cash today — non-recourse receivables financing on Hedera.
description:
Freelancers who invoice clients abroad wait 30 to 60 days to get paid, and have no way to
borrow against that invoice while they wait. Banks won't underwrite a $2,000 receivable
from a sole trader in Malang — the diligence costs more than the loan.

Forfait tokenizes an unpaid invoice as a zero-coupon bond using Hedera's Asset Tokenization
Studio. Face value is the invoice amount, maturity is the due date. A funder buys it at a
discount today; when the client pays at maturity, settlement and distribution execute
automatically. Every state change — submitted, verified, funded, paid, settled — is written
to the Hedera Consensus Service as a tamper-evident audit trail, while the invoice document
itself stays off-chain and only its hash is published.

This is forfaiting: the non-recourse purchase of cross-border receivables at a discount. It
is a century-old trade finance instrument. Forfait makes it work at ticket sizes where the
paperwork used to cost more than the deal.
how_its_made:
The security token is issued through Asset Tokenization Studio (ERC-1400) on Hedera's EVM
layer, using the ATS SDK rather than hand-rolled contracts — so compliance controls like
control lists, KYC gating, pause, and transfer restrictions come from audited code rather
than from me.

Maturity settlement uses Hedera Scheduled Transactions with setWaitForExpiry, so the network
itself executes the payout on the due date. No cron job, no keeper bot, nothing to keep
running. The 62-day ceiling on scheduled transactions is why the product accepts invoices
with terms of 60 days or less.

The audit trail runs on the Hedera Consensus Service: one topic, one message per lifecycle
event, ordered and hash-chained by consensus. Invoice documents never touch the ledger —
only a SHA-256 hash, so a funder can verify the document they were shown is the one that was
financed, without the pricing becoming public.

Privy provides authentication and embedded wallets, so a freelancer signs in with an email
and never handles a seed phrase. Reads go through the Hedera Mirror Node REST API.

Fees are why this works at ticket sizes banks ignore: I measured a transfer at $0.0001 and
an HCS message at $0.00017 on testnet. Financing a $2,000 invoice costs a fraction of a cent
in ledger fees.
auto_summary: A web app tokenizes invoices on Hedera as ATS-issued receivable bonds, logs lifecycle events to HCS, and schedules maturity settlement.
